VI. ANY ADVERSE ENVIRONMENTAL EFFECTS WHICH CANNOT BE AVOIDED SHOULD THIS PROPOSED BE IMPLEMENTED.
1. Environmental Effects, Physical
Adverse effects, due to project construction in the execution period, will increase noise levels, air pollution levels, soil erosion, and water pollution, to some minor degree. Measures built into the urban renewal plan and provided under the local city codes will keep levels to a minimum. Since all of the various types of construction will not occur in any one single time period, during the 5 year life of the project, a number of the minor adverse elements will not combine to cause a serious problem.
Solid waste generated by demolition will be consumed by the new Harrisburg incinerator, which is presently being used at only a fraction of its total capacity. It operates at a high rate of effiency and will lessen the danger of excess air pollution from the disposal of project generated refuse.
The possibility of water main or sewer failure after the streets have been repaired (as part of the project activity) is a gamble that will have to be taken. Additional Federal funds to expand the scope of urban renewal activities in flood disaster areas; namely extensive repair or replacement of underground utilities, is not likely due to the overall demand on available funds for basic essential program items, i.e., relocation assistance, repair of public utilities, flood plain clearance, etc.
However, since the threat of utility failure and subsequent street excavation is only a possibility, the needed street surface repairs can not be delayed or passed over because of the possibility. The relocation of families, individuals and businesses in the area is inevitable if flood plain management is to be effective. The objective of the plan is to remove structures from areas where flooding will occur most frequently and to generally decrease the population density of the area. This can not be done without a certain amount of relocation. In some cases individuals are eager to relocate from their flood damaged property.
2. Environmental Effects, Socio-economic
As mentioned previously, the displacees will be eligible for the various types of relocation assistance discribed in Part I. Of major concern, is whether or not facilities for relocation will be available when needed. The application for urban renewal indicates that the Harrisburg Redevelopment Authority has conducted a thorough analysis of the local housing market.
